description: PSAT, the Power System Analysis Toolbox, is a MATLAB toolbox for electric power system analysis and simulation, created and maintained by Federico Milano at University College Dublin; its command-line version is also compatible with GNU Octave. It offers power flow, continuation power flow, optimal power flow, small signal stability analysis and time domain simulation, with a complete graphical user interface, a Simulink-based library for network design, user-defined models, FACTS and wind turbine models, conversion of data files from several formats, export of results to EPS, plain text, Excel and LaTeX, and interfaces to the GAMS and UWPFLOW programs. Coverage is generic: any transmission network the user builds or imports. Access: zip archives for MATLAB and Octave for versions 2.1.2 to 2.1.11 are downloaded from the page; the last update is 4 April 2022. Licence and cost: distributed free of charge under the GPL with no warranty; the full PSAT manual is no longer free and must be requested or purchased. Caveats: a single-developer project on a commercial MATLAB base, with no update since 2022. It suits stability, voltage collapse and cascading outage studies on small and medium grids, alongside MATPOWER and OpenDSS catalogued here.
